topics.title: Investor brief
topics.question: What should the property accomplish without relying on appreciation?
flags: A return target without a time horizon
topics.action: Write a one-page brief with an acceptable downside and a decision owner.
topics.limit: A brief guides your search; it cannot establish suitability.
checks: Write a one-page brief with an acceptable downside and a decision owner.

topics.title: Cash allocation
topics.question: How much cash remains after closing and setup?
flags: Reserves counted as spendable purchase cash
topics.action: Separate committed cash from the reserve that must remain available.
topics.limit: An allocation worksheet does not establish loan eligibility.
checks: Separate committed cash from the reserve that must remain available.

topics.title: Lender comparison
topics.question: Are the loan offers comparable on amount, term and total cost?
topics.action: Request matching assumptions and document remaining differences.
topics.limit: Consumer mortgage resources may not apply to business-purpose loans.
checks: Request matching assumptions and document remaining differences.

topics.title: Loan conditions
topics.question: Which financing conditions remain unresolved?
flags: A prequalification treated as final approval
topics.action: Ask the lender to identify the owner and evidence needed for each condition.
topics.limit: Only the lender can confirm its current approval and requirements.
checks: Ask the lender to identify the owner and evidence needed for each condition.

topics.title: Closing cash
topics.question: Does the available cash cover the actual closing requirement?
topics.action: Reconcile deposits and credits to the latest dated closing estimate.
topics.limit: Confirm final settlement amounts with the responsible closing professionals.
checks: Reconcile deposits and credits to the latest dated closing estimate.

topics.title: Seller records
topics.question: Which operating claims have original records behind them?
topics.action: Request source files with the reporting period and definition of revenue.
topics.limit: Access to records does not prove their completeness or accuracy.
checks: Request source files with the reporting period and definition of revenue.

topics.title: Comparable selection
topics.question: Why does each comparison property belong in the set?
topics.action: Create an inclusion rule before selecting comparable properties.
topics.limit: A comparable set does not predict a particular property's results.
checks: Create an inclusion rule before selecting comparable properties.

topics.title: Seasonality review
topics.question: Does the model include a full operating cycle?
flags: launch months treated as stable operations
topics.action: Plot the months separately and annotate unavailable periods.
topics.limit: Historic seasonality is context rather than a future forecast.
checks: Plot the months separately and annotate unavailable periods.

topics.title: Availability plan
topics.question: How many nights are realistically offered for bookings?
flags: Owner stays left in available inventory
topics.action: Separate available, booked, owner-used and closed nights.
topics.limit: A calendar cannot explain every unbooked night without context.
checks: Separate available, booked, owner-used and closed nights.

topics.title: Revenue definitions
topics.question: Are room charges separated from taxes and pass-through receipts?
flags: Collected taxes included as earned room revenue
topics.action: Write a reconciliation from room charges to payouts.
topics.limit: Definitions must match before two income figures can be compared.
checks: Write a reconciliation from room charges to payouts.

topics.title: Property restrictions
topics.question: Who will establish the restrictions applying to this exact property?
flags: A neighboring property treated as permission
topics.action: Record the exact authority, property reference and unresolved question.
topics.limit: This workflow does not determine local legality or interpret restrictions.
checks: Record the exact authority, property reference and unresolved question.

topics.title: Insurance scope
topics.question: Does the quoted policy address the proposed use?
flags: Ordinary occupancy assumed to cover rental activity
topics.action: Describe the planned use to the insurer and request written answers.
topics.limit: Only the insurer and qualified advisers can confirm coverage.
checks: Describe the planned use to the insurer and request written answers.

topics.title: Inspection scope
topics.question: Which systems are inside and outside the inspection scope?
topics.action: Record exclusions and assign follow-up specialists before closing decisions.
topics.limit: A planning worksheet is not an inspection or safety certification.
checks: Record exclusions and assign follow-up specialists before closing decisions.

topics.title: Roof review
topics.question: What evidence addresses roof condition and near-term work?
flags: A recent patch described as a new roof
age used instead of condition evidence
topics.action: Separate observed defects from estimated remaining life and request a scoped quote.
topics.limit: Qualified inspection is needed for property-specific conclusions.
checks: Separate observed defects from estimated remaining life and request a scoped quote.

topics.title: Heating and cooling
topics.question: Can the proposed system support the intended operating pattern?
flags: Service date confused with replacement date
topics.action: Ask a qualified technician to identify condition, scope and any quoted work.
topics.limit: No worksheet determines system safety, capacity or code compliance.
checks: Ask a qualified technician to identify condition, scope and any quoted work.

topics.title: Plumbing review
topics.question: Which visible issues require specialist investigation?
flags: A stain dismissed without tracing its source
topics.action: Document the observation and request a written specialist follow-up.
topics.limit: Do not treat a visual checklist as a diagnosis.
checks: Document the observation and request a written specialist follow-up.

topics.title: Electrical review
topics.question: What electrical questions remain open after inspection?
flags: An outlet test treated as a whole-system assessment
topics.action: Keep observed issues separate from work recommendations and approvals.
topics.limit: A licensed professional must address electrical safety and required work.
checks: Keep observed issues separate from work recommendations and approvals.

topics.title: Moisture follow-up
topics.question: Has the source of observed moisture been investigated?
flags: Cosmetic covering treated as source correction
topics.action: Record where moisture was observed and request appropriate investigation.
topics.limit: This page offers document planning, not health advice or remediation instructions.
checks: Record where moisture was observed and request appropriate investigation.

topics.title: Water supply
topics.question: What supports assumptions about the property's water service?
flags: Supply capacity assumed from bedroom count
topics.action: Record the source and ask the appropriate provider or specialist about open issues.
topics.limit: Testing and service requirements vary and need property-specific review.
checks: Record the source and ask the appropriate provider or specialist about open issues.

topics.title: Wastewater systems
topics.question: What records describe the wastewater system and its limitations?
flags: Guest capacity inferred without system review
topics.action: Ask an appropriate specialist which records and checks are needed.
topics.limit: No capacity or compliance conclusion is made here.
checks: Ask an appropriate specialist which records and checks are needed.

topics.title: Internet service
topics.question: Is usable service confirmed at the exact address?
flags: Area coverage treated as address availability
advertised speed treated as a guarantee
topics.action: Confirm address service, installation costs and a practical backup plan.
topics.limit: Provider availability and performance must be verified directly.
checks: Confirm address service, installation costs and a practical backup plan.

topics.title: Parking plan
topics.question: How will guests arrive and park without relying on assumptions?
flags: Listing capacity unsupported by usable spaces
topics.action: Map the arrival path and verify applicable restrictions with responsible parties.
topics.limit: This plan does not establish permitted occupancy or parking rights.
checks: Map the arrival path and verify applicable restrictions with responsible parties.

topics.title: Accessibility information
topics.question: Which property features can be described accurately to guests?
flags: Broad accessibility labels without supporting detail
topics.action: Describe specific verified features and identify questions needing specialist advice.
topics.limit: Do not claim accessibility certification or legal compliance from this worksheet.
checks: Describe specific verified features and identify questions needing specialist advice.

topics.title: Noise management
topics.question: Who handles a guest or neighbor noise concern?
topics.action: Document response responsibilities and appropriate communication channels.
topics.limit: Local rules and device/privacy requirements need separate review.
checks: Document response responsibilities and appropriate communication channels.

topics.title: Amenity scope
topics.question: What does each proposed amenity cost to install and operate?
flags: Purchase price treated as total cost
topics.action: Combine installation, ongoing cost and operating responsibility in one scope.
topics.limit: An amenity's popularity does not establish incremental profit.
checks: Combine installation, ongoing cost and operating responsibility in one scope.

topics.title: Pool service
topics.question: Who owns inspection, maintenance and incident response for a pool?
flags: A service visit treated as safety certification
topics.action: Request written scope and identify the qualified parties for open questions.
topics.limit: This is a responsibility worksheet, not pool safety guidance.
checks: Request written scope and identify the qualified parties for open questions.

topics.title: Furnishing budget
topics.question: Is the room-by-room budget complete and deliverable?
topics.action: Reconcile quantities and landed costs to the total setup allowance.
topics.limit: Hypothetical allowances are not contractor or vendor quotes.
checks: Reconcile quantities and landed costs to the total setup allowance.

topics.title: Delivery dependencies
topics.question: Which deliveries can delay installation or launch?
topics.action: Identify critical items and an alternative if a delivery slips.
topics.limit: Lead times must be confirmed with the current vendor.
checks: Identify critical items and an alternative if a delivery slips.

topics.title: Repair scope
topics.question: Can multiple quotes be compared on the same work?
topics.action: Normalize the scope before comparing totals and flag exclusions.
topics.limit: A low estimate does not establish condition or an adequate scope.
checks: Normalize the scope before comparing totals and flag exclusions.

topics.title: Setup contingency
topics.question: How much room is left for unpriced setup work?
flags: Same contingency counted in several buckets
topics.action: Keep contingency separate and assign a quote request to each unknown.
topics.limit: Contingency size is a scenario choice rather than a universal standard.
checks: Keep contingency separate and assign a quote request to each unknown.

topics.title: Management handoff
topics.question: What must be delivered to the operator after closing?
flags: Acquisition scope confused with ongoing management
topics.action: Create a handoff checklist with recipients and acceptance evidence.
topics.limit: The signed agreements govern responsibilities.
checks: Create a handoff checklist with recipients and acceptance evidence.

topics.title: Cleaning operations
topics.question: Who owns turnover quality, linen stock and exception handling?
topics.action: Specify billing units and who handles a failed or late turnover.
topics.limit: A checklist does not certify sanitation or vendor performance.
checks: Specify billing units and who handles a failed or late turnover.

topics.title: Maintenance coverage
topics.question: How are routine requests and urgent repairs assigned?
flags: no contact when primary vendor is unavailable
topics.action: Document the approval workflow and provider backup.
topics.limit: Use qualified providers for property-specific work.
checks: Document the approval workflow and provider backup.

topics.title: Listing readiness
topics.question: Which published claims have been checked against the property?
flags: Stock photos used as property evidence
topics.action: Mark each listing statement verified, pending or excluded before publication.
topics.limit: Accurate descriptions still require ongoing updates.
checks: Mark each listing statement verified, pending or excluded before publication.

topics.title: Booking channel setup
topics.question: Who owns the accounts, calendar links and payout destination?
flags: Shared credentials treated as a handoff
topics.action: Document authorized ownership and test the normal booking workflow.
topics.limit: Do not record passwords or private payout details in this public worksheet.
checks: Document authorized ownership and test the normal booking workflow.

topics.title: Operating reserve
topics.question: What ongoing obligations can the cash reserve absorb?
flags: Reserve included in a return denominator but unavailable to operations
topics.action: Model a shortfall and distinguish earmarked funds from usable reserve.
topics.limit: Runway is arithmetic under assumptions, not a recommended reserve level.
checks: Model a shortfall and distinguish earmarked funds from usable reserve.

topics.title: Owner reporting
topics.question: Which recurring report connects income, expenses and cash?
topics.action: Agree on reporting dates and preserve a bridge from source records to totals.
topics.limit: A management report is not an audit opinion.
checks: Agree on reporting dates and preserve a bridge from source records to totals.

topics.title: Exit flexibility
topics.question: What alternatives remain if the original operating plan changes?
flags: Future sale value treated as certain
topics.action: Document unverified alternatives and the checks needed before relying on them.
topics.limit: This workflow does not forecast value or confirm alternate-use rights.
checks: Document unverified alternatives and the checks needed before relying on them.

topics.title: Adviser coordination
topics.question: Which questions require the lender, inspector, attorney or tax adviser?
flags: One provider assumed to cover every specialty
topics.action: Assign each unresolved question to the appropriate qualified party.
topics.limit: Acquisition support is not a substitute for specialist professional advice.
checks: Assign each unresolved question to the appropriate qualified party.

topics.title: Final decision record
topics.question: Can you explain the purchase decision from the retained evidence?
topics.action: Record the basis, remaining uncertainty and conditions before deciding.
topics.limit: The owner remains responsible for their decision and advisers.
checks: Record the basis, remaining uncertainty and conditions before deciding.

references.title: Source register
references.question: Why keep one register for evidence?
references.intro: A register connects a document to its date, origin, scope and owner. Use a stable reference rather than renaming an attachment whenever a new version arrives.
references.action: Give every important assumption a source ID. Mark missing records explicitly and record the next request beside them.
references.limit: An attachment list alone does not show whether a document supports a particular claim.

references.title: Decision gates
references.question: How can a project use explicit review gates?
references.intro: A gate is a condition that must be resolved before a chosen commitment. It differs from a calendar reminder because completion needs evidence.
references.action: Separate gates about funding, property permission, condition and operating readiness. Give each one an owner and a defined output.
references.limit: A completed task is not permission to proceed if its result exposes a new issue.

references.title: Scope matrix
references.question: How do you compare who does what?
references.intro: A scope matrix places tasks beside responsible parties, deliverables and exclusions. It helps reveal where an acquisition service stops and another provider begins.
references.action: Use actual proposal language when recording responsibilities. Mark conflicting descriptions rather than choosing the most convenient one.
references.limit: Marketing descriptions do not replace your agreement.

references.title: Assumption register
references.question: What belongs beside every estimate?
references.intro: Record the value, units, period, source and reason the estimate is being used. Keep the previous value when a revision changes the decision.
references.action: Separate recorded history from a forecast and note which inputs move together in a downside case.
references.limit: A well-documented assumption can still be wrong.

references.title: Quote normalization
references.question: How can quotes be made comparable?
references.intro: Two quotes may price different quantities, materials, access conditions or exclusions. Comparing totals first can hide those differences.
references.action: Build one common scope and ask each provider to identify its included and excluded items against that scope.
references.limit: Do not convert an allowance into a fixed price without the provider's confirmation.

references.title: Version control
references.question: How do you avoid reviewing an old proposal?
references.intro: A stable document name with a visible version date and status helps distinguish draft, superseded and current records.
references.action: Keep a change log of the values or scope items altered. Link the approved version from the decision record.
references.limit: The latest file received is not necessarily the operative agreement.

references.title: Responsibility assignment
references.question: How do you make an open question actionable?
references.intro: A question needs one owner, a requested response and a date for follow-up. Several people being copied does not establish ownership.
references.action: Ask the owner to identify evidence of completion rather than simply marking the question answered.
references.limit: Assigning responsibility does not expand a provider's professional scope.

references.title: Document completeness
references.question: What does a complete file mean for a decision?
references.intro: Completeness depends on the question. A full booking export may support room revenue while saying nothing about repairs or financing.
references.action: Define the minimum fields and time range needed before requesting documents. Log omitted periods and inaccessible attachments.
references.limit: A complete set can still contain inaccuracies or conflicting definitions.

references.title: Chronology
references.question: Why sequence records by observation date?
references.intro: The date a fact was observed can differ from a document's issue date or the date it was received. All three can matter.
references.action: Place events in order and connect later revisions to the records they replace.
references.limit: An old condition report does not establish current condition.

references.title: Budget ownership
references.question: Who changes a project allowance?
references.intro: A budget owner decides which estimate is current and records the reason for revisions. Without that role, multiple totals can circulate.
references.action: Keep original allowance, current quote, approved change and funded amount in separate fields.
references.limit: A spending cap does not guarantee that vendors can deliver the work.

references.title: Contingency register
references.question: How should unknown costs be tracked?
references.intro: An unknown cost is different from a zero cost. List its scope, the reason it is unresolved and the party expected to price it.
references.action: Avoid distributing the same contingency across several totals. Show where reserve funds can and cannot be used.
references.limit: A contingency is a planning choice, not a guarantee against overruns.

references.title: Timeline dependencies
references.question: What makes a launch schedule credible?
references.intro: A dependency connects a task to prerequisites such as access, delivery or approval. A target date without prerequisites is difficult to evaluate.
references.action: Identify the critical sequence and a fallback if one predecessor slips. Keep vendor lead times separate from internal work time.
references.limit: A schedule does not establish availability or approval.

references.title: Communication log
references.question: What should be retained from a project call?
references.intro: Record decisions, open questions, responsible parties and promised documents. A long transcript can be less useful than a clear action record.
references.action: Confirm material scope or price changes with the appropriate party in writing.
references.limit: Your notes do not amend an agreement by themselves.

references.title: Data minimization
references.question: What should stay out of a planning worksheet?
references.intro: Use document references rather than copying account numbers, identification details, passwords or private client information into general notes.
references.action: Keep original sensitive records in your own appropriate secure storage and use a non-sensitive reference in the workbook.
references.limit: A browser-local worksheet is not a secure document vault.

references.title: Field definitions
references.question: Why agree on terminology before comparing figures?
references.intro: Revenue, cash flow, fees and occupancy can refer to different measures. Definitions tell the reader which transactions and costs are included.
references.action: Write a short data dictionary with units, period and exclusions. Reconcile measures before comparing them.
references.limit: Matching labels do not prove that two underlying calculations match.

references.title: Exception tracking
references.question: How do you retain unresolved differences?
references.intro: An exception log preserves the original conflicting values, their sources and the question needed to reconcile them.
references.action: Assign a follow-up and keep the item open until a response addresses the actual mismatch.
references.limit: Do not mark a conflict resolved merely because one source is newer.

references.title: Evidence handoff
references.question: How should one provider transfer a project file?
references.intro: A handoff needs a manifest of the records delivered, recipient access and acknowledgment of anything still missing.
references.action: Use stable links and verify the recipient can open the required documents. Record who owns future updates.
references.limit: Sharing a folder is not proof that the intended records are readable or complete.

references.title: Change impact
references.question: What else changes when one assumption moves?
references.intro: A revised nightly rate can change revenue, fees, cash flow and returns. A delayed launch can change both costs and available nights.
references.action: Trace the dependent outputs and preserve the prior scenario for comparison.
references.limit: Updating a headline result without updating dependent assumptions creates an inconsistent model.

references.title: Readiness review
references.question: How do you distinguish ready from almost ready?
references.intro: Readiness is a defined set of completed checks with evidence. It should be specific to the task rather than a single broad status.
references.action: Review blockers separately from tasks that can finish later and document the basis for each classification.
references.limit: This workflow does not certify safety, legality or investment suitability.

references.title: Research prioritization
references.question: Which open questions should be answered first?
references.intro: Prioritize questions that could change whether the property can be used, funded or operated as intended. Resolve costly uncertainty before polishing minor estimates.
references.action: Record decision impact, the party needed and the effort to obtain evidence. Reassess priorities when a new issue appears.
references.limit: Priority is a planning judgment rather than a promise of an optimal purchase.
